t: Listen to a talk in a history class.
Construction of the Erie Canal began in 1817, and many people thought the project was foolish.
But when the canal opened in 1825, it connected the Great Lakes to the Atlantic Ocean through New York.
Shipping costs between the Midwest and New York City fell by about ninety percent, and New York became the country's leading port.
The canal's success didn't last forever, though.
By the 1850s, railroads could move goods faster and all year round, while the canal froze in winter.
So traffic on the canal gradually declined.
